# The command line

```
usage: drawspec [-h] [--version] {render,validate,theme,schema} ...
```

Nothing is printed to stdout but the thing that was asked for — the SVG, the
schema, or a one-line confirmation — so `drawspec render doc.json > doc.svg`
is safe. Refusals go to stderr **in full**: the message names the remedy as
well as the fault, and a build script that truncates it to a summary line is a
build script whose author ends up guessing.

## Exit codes

The split is worth stating: **2 is about the invocation, 1 is about the
content.** A misspelt flag or an unknown profile is 2 — nothing was read, so
nothing can be said about it. A document that cannot be read, cannot be parsed,
or cannot be fitted is 1, and a refusal is an outcome, not a crash.

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | It worked. |
| `1` | The document, the theme or the fit was refused. |
| `2` | The command line itself was wrong. |

## Commands

### `drawspec render`

Read a document, draw it, and write the SVG to stdout or to a file.

```
usage: drawspec render [-h] [-o OUT] [--theme THEME] [--width WIDTH]
                       [--height HEIGHT] [--profile {inline,standalone}]
                       document
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `document` | The document to render. |
| `-o`, `--out` | Write here instead of stdout. |
| `--theme` | A bundled theme name or a theme file. |
| `--width` | Override the document's width. |
| `--height` | Override the document's height. |
| `--profile` | The embedding profile. One of `inline`, `standalone`. Default `inline`. |

### `drawspec validate`

Parse and check a document, drawing nothing. Every violation is printed with the JSON pointer of the place it was written.

```
usage: drawspec validate [-h] [--theme THEME] document
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `document` | The document to validate. |
| `--theme` | A bundled theme name or a theme file. |

### `drawspec theme`

Tools for the files that decide appearance.

```
usage: drawspec theme [-h] {check} ...
```

#### `drawspec theme check`

Load a theme and run its invariants, the greyscale role pairing included.

```
usage: drawspec theme check [-h] theme
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `theme` | A bundled theme name or a theme file. |

### `drawspec schema`

Write the published document JSON Schema, for editor completion.

```
usage: drawspec schema [-h] [--out OUT]
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--out` | Write here instead of stdout. |

## Embedding profiles

`render --profile` takes `inline`, `standalone`.

* **`inline`** — for pasting into a Markdown or HTML page. Strokes are
  `currentColor`, so the drawing inherits the page's ink and follows it into
  dark mode; there is no `<style>` block to leak, and every id is scoped so two
  diagrams on one page cannot collide.
* **`standalone`** — for a linked `.svg`, a PDF conversion, or anywhere there
  is nothing to inherit from. `currentColor` is resolved to the theme's
  `[canvas] ink`, because a converter's own default is not a design decision.

## Themes

`--theme` takes a bundled theme name or the path of a TOML file. See
[the theme reference](theme.md) for every key a theme may set, and
[the guide](guide.md) for how to write one.
